text: The purchaser will likely prevail because the recorded easement appurtenant attached to the woman's land and automatically passed with her title when she sold it to the man. Although the easement temporarily merged into his single ownership, selling the house severed that merger, causing the burdened status of the highway-side lot to remain while the benefit followed the new owner of the dominant parcel. Consequently, the purchaser holds a valid right-of-way that the seller cannot extinguish by erecting a barricade without providing an alternative route or compensation. CONFIDENCE: 95
